questions.q: For the arithmetic sequence with $a_1=6$ and common difference $d=4$, find $a_{12}$.
For the arithmetic sequence with $a_1=20$ and $d=-3$, find $a_{15}$.
A geometric sequence has $a_1=3$ and each term is $2$ times the previous one. Find the smallest $n$ for which $a_n=384$.
Find $S_{12}$ for the arithmetic sequence with $a_1=6$, $d=4$ (using $a_{12}=50$ from above).
Find $S_8$ for the arithmetic sequence with $a_1=2$, $d=5$.
For the geometric sequence with $a_1=4$ and common ratio $r=3$, find $a_6$.
A geometric sequence begins $5, -10, 20, -40,\ldots$. Find $r$ and $a_7$.
Find $S_6$ for the geometric sequence with $a_1=4$, $r=3$ (using $a_6=972$ from above).
Find the sum of the infinite geometric series $20+\dfrac{20}{3}+\dfrac{20}{9}+\cdots$.
questions.answer: $a=20$, $r=\dfrac{1}{3}$, and $|r|<1$, so by Theorem 3.2 the sum is $\dfrac{20}{1-\frac{1}{3}}=\dfrac{20}{\frac{2}{3}}=30$.

questions.q: Find the sum of the infinite geometric series $9-3+1-\dfrac{1}{3}+\cdots$.
Explain why the infinite geometric series with $a=5$, $r=2$ has no finite sum.
questions.answer: Theorem 3.2 requires $|r|<1$ for the partial sums to converge. Here $|r|=2>1$, so the terms grow without bound and the series diverges — it has no finite sum.
